To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“The stream macroinvertebrates in the two major watershers in Mongolia are structured by hydrological connectivity and differ in the community structure, guild composition and vulnerability to climate change”.
“Stream invertebrate community structure in Mongolia’s two major watershends is determined by hydrological connectivity and the magnitude of climate change expected to occur in each of them.”
the stream macroinverterbrate community structure of the Central Asian Internal Watersheds is more nested, more distinct, more stable and less resilient than that of the Arctic Ocean Watersheds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the vulnerability of stream ecosystems to climate change.
the current structure and expected future changes of stream communities in a changing environment.
the vulnerability of stream communities and the consequences of ongoing and upcoming environmental changes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stream communities of the two watershends are different in their structure and that they are likely to change differently under climate change.
the stream communities in Mongolia will change due to climate change and the magnitude of the changes will differ between the watersheds.
the Mongolian riverine macroinvertebrate fauna is a unique combination of the Central Asian and Arctic biogeographical realms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the communities in the two major watershederas of Mongolia are different in terms of taxonomic and functional structure, and the communities in the CAIW are more vulnerable to the upcoming impacts of climate changes.
the communities’ structure of Mongolia’s stream macroinvertebrates is determined not only by climate but also by hydrological connectivity.

the Mongolian stream communities are expected to be affected by the upcoming climate change, but in a different manner, depending on their location in the country and on their hydrological connectivity to other drainages.
The main takeaway from our work is that

conservation strategies for the Mongolian stream communities should be based on watershed level planning, as the communities are highly differentiated and the expected climate change will affect them differently.
the hydrological connectivity among sub-drainages of the same watersheds is an important element for structuring stream macroinvertebrates.
the stream communities in the AOW are less diverse and less connected, and therefore more sensitive to climate change than the communities of the CAIW.
